Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

after the review please save the updated sheet in the shared folder and print one copy for the front cupboard use the date of the review rather than the date the group first asked for access if a room is still being repaired show that clearly rather than guessing when it will reopen the final paragraph of the note should say who is responsible for the next check and when it is due currently I can check it on the ninth of october if Ivo confirms the fob is back by monday morning otherwise we will need to check the cupboard with the building manager before the evening group starts and I do not want the printed sheet to imply that the fob has been returned until we have that confirmation", "output": "We need to update the shared studio access list before the new printmaking group starts on the first Monday in October. The studio is in the old ferry warehouse on Birch Lane, and the entrance is the blue door beside the loading bay. The list is not a record of who owns a key; it shows who may enter and which rooms they can use. Please keep that distinction clear, because the building manager checks the access list against the alarm log every Friday afternoon, and he has asked us not to leave old permissions in place just because somebody still has a brass key.

On the current sheet there are twenty-three names and four people who have left the cooperative. Last spring, we added the ceramics room and the quiet edit room, so the room column needs to stay beside each name rather than moving into a note at the bottom. Please spell the new platform TideBoard exactly like that, because the invite will point to its access page. We are still using the paper copy clipped inside the front cupboard as a backup, and the copy should show the date it was checked, the person who checked it, and the next review date.

For the new group, we have six members and one visiting tutor. The tutor can enter the main studio and the wash-up room, but not the equipment cage unless a staff member is present. The cage has the large paper cutter and the spare drying racks, and the insurance note says a visitor cannot be left alone in there. The group is booked Tuesday and Thursday evenings from six until nine, and they can arrive fifteen minutes early to set up, but they should not use the space before five forty-five even if the outside door happens to be unlocked.

For the weekend keyholder, put Ivo as weekend keyholder. Mara is coordinating the open day, but she is not carrying the alarm fob. Ivo has agreed to lock up on Saturday and Sunday this month, and his access should include the main studio, the wash-up room, and the front cupboard, but not the office. The alarm fob stays in a numbered envelope in the cupboard when it is not with him. On Monday morning, he will return it to the envelope and text me that the cupboard is locked.

We should also fix the entries for people who need occasional access rather than weekly access:
1. Nessa is coming in on the twelfth of October to collect her framed maps. She needs the front cupboard and the main studio for that visit only.
2. Pavel will check the extraction fan on the nineteenth and needs the main studio plus the equipment cage while he is testing it.
3. Lian can enter the edit room on weekday afternoons, but only after she has booked a time on the TideBoard calendar. Her booking is not permission to enter the other rooms.
4. Jo can use the wash-up room during the community class on the twenty-sixth, but should not be given a standing permission after that evening.

We have had some confusion about the side entrance because the delivery company props it open when they bring clay on Wednesdays. Please do not copy that practice for group members. If somebody arrives while the blue door is locked, they should use the bell marked “studio” and wait for a member to meet them. The bell works, but it takes about ten seconds before it rings at the front desk. If the class tutor is carrying supplies and cannot get to the door, the tutor can ask the person to wait outside rather than share a door code. We have not issued individual codes to this group, and the temporary delivery code expires at the end of September.

There are two people whose access depends on a condition that could change later. Priya may keep her edit room permission if the soundproofing work finishes by the second of October. If the contractor is still working then, please leave her name on the list but mark the permission as pending, and do not give her a date to use the room until we confirm the room is open. That matters because she is preparing audio for the neighborhood oral history project and has already reserved a microphone from the library. The other person is Oren, who can enter the main studio while he is supervising the kiln delivery. If the delivery is postponed, his access should not start early just because his name appears on the general list.

Before sending invitations, compare each room entry with the notes from the meeting and remove permissions belonging to the four former members, but do not remove their names from the archived copy. The archived copy is kept in the locked drawer in the office, and only the access coordinator and the building manager can read it. For the working list, add a small note that the visiting tutor has no equipment cage access unless accompanied, and that Nessa's visit ends when she has collected the maps. The list should not show the alarm code or anybody's personal phone number, because that information is stored separately.

After the review, please save the updated sheet in the shared folder and print one copy for the front cupboard. Use the date of the review rather than the date the group first asked for access. If a room is still being repaired, show that clearly rather than guessing when it will reopen. The final paragraph of the note should say who is responsible for the next check and when it is due. Currently, I can check it on the ninth of October if Ivo confirms the fob is back by Monday morning. Otherwise, we will need to check the cupboard with the building manager before the evening group starts, and I do not want the printed sheet to imply that the fob has been returned until we have that confirmation."}]
